summary: Reproduced 518.307x pickle amplification from CPU tensor views created by get_new_expanded_mm_items. CPU tensor slices are now cloned at split time, including feature, precomputed_embeddings, and split tensor metadata, while accelerator slices remain views for IPC/shared-memory paths. The exact fixture now measures 1.312x amplification.

tests.what_was_measured: Before: 512 split image items, 1,048,576 logical feature bytes, 543,484,451 pickle bytes, 518.307x amplification, and 1,048,576-byte storage retained by a 2,048-byte slice. After: 1,375,278 pickle bytes, 1.312x amplification, and 2,048-byte storage for the 2,048-byte slice.

9 tests passed, covering pickle size and owned storage for CPU feature slices, precomputed embeddings, item- and feature-aligned tensor metadata, plus existing image grid, numpy, fallback, and pass-through boundaries. The two new regression tests failed before the source correction.

On AMD Instinct MI355X with ROCm/HIP 7.2.26015, an accelerator slice matched an independent expected tensor and retained the parent's storage pointer, confirming the CPU-only materialization boundary.

gpu_execution.evidence: reports/j-b90e4216b064/gpu-validation.txt records AMD Instinct MI355X, correct slice values, and shared parent storage for the accelerator path.

remaining_limitations: No model weights or multimodal serving workload were used; validation targets the reported deterministic splitting and pickle serialization path directly.
The source report used CUDA H200 hardware; accelerator boundary validation here used the assigned single AMD Instinct MI355X with ROCm. Pickling behavior under test is CPU-side.
No native code changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
